_readme: Lounge version manifest. Served by serve_nocache.py from C:\NEXUS on port 8899,
so both the web app and the Android app fetch it from the SAME host they were
loaded from: http://<host>:8899/apk/version.json  (web uses the relative path).
Not a relay endpoint on purpose. This is public, read-only, non-personal data --
gating it behind X-Nexus-Pin would add a CORS preflight and a failure mode to a
poll that must work on a TV that may never have had the relay configured. The
PIN-gated relay stays for /play, /control and /reel (real actions, personal data).
serve_nocache.py sends Cache-Control: no-store on everything, so an update check
can never be answered from a stale browser cache. That is the whole reason this
file lives here rather than beside a CDN.
WHEN YOU SHIP: bump latest.android.* to match build.gradle.kts, bump
latest.web.cacheName to match CACHE_NAME in sw.js, and prepend a changelog entry.
The web app compares latest.web.cacheName against its own LOUNGE_BUILD constant;
the Android app compares latest.android.versionCode against BuildConfig.VERSION_CODE.

Live-verified against the actually-deployed proxy (not a local mock): manifest request returns 200 + correct application/dash+xml + wildcard ACAO with real MPD content; a real segment URL returns 200 + video/mp4 + wildcard ACAO with 204KB of real segment bytes; an arbitrary non-TVNZ URL is correctly rejected with 400. Blind motion judge re-run against this exact build (motion-lounge-transitions-v158-washfix, 2026-08-20T20:54): OVERALLS [7,7,6] MEDIAN 7, up from the pre-fix [4,7,4] MEDIAN 4. changelog.title: Intro dolly rebuilt as true 2.5D parallax -- 3 depth layers, not 1
changes: Researched real camera-department technique before rebuilding (Deep's explicit ask): a dolly shot reads as depth because near and far objects move at DIFFERENT rates as the camera travels -- that differential is what an eye reads as "distance". v151's portal-out scaled the whole #intro overlay as one rigid block, which is a zoom with easing, not a camera move, no matter how it's dressed up.

Rebuilt across the DOM's existing 3 depth planes, sharing one CSS perspective declared on the shared parent so they read as one continuous 3D space instead of 3 independent zooms: starfield (farthest, scale 1->1.12, 1.5px blur), projector rays (mid, 1->1.55, 5px blur), couch/tagline/mark -- the actual subject (nearest, 1->2.6 + rotationX tilt + z-push, 11px blur, same numbers v151 used but now isolated to the one layer meant to be close).

Verified live by directly seeking the real GSAP timeline mid-push (not simulated): captured a genuine screenshot showing sharp background stars, moderately-soft mid-ground rays, and a heavily-blurred foreground mark simultaneously in one frame -- real depth-of-field, not a uniform blur. judge_harness floor unchanged at 9.64/10, 0 new console errors.

changelog.title: Real fix: Matrix-drop scramble was starting mid-popcorn-burst, competing for frames with 16 simultaneous kernel animations

Root cause found by actually computing the timeline's own numbers: the tagline decode (SETTLE) used to start at POP_CLIMAX+0.44, but the 16-kernel popcorn burst (32 simultaneous tweens: each kernel has its own rise+fall animation, staggered 35ms apart) doesn't finish until POP_CLIMAX+~1.25 -- so the decode's ~85 scheduled character mutations were competing for paint time against 32 other active animations for almost the entire scramble window.

Fixed by pushing SETTLE to POP_CLIMAX+1.35, after the popcorn burst is fully finished, giving the decode a clear runway. Every other intro beat (Enter fade-in, the pause, portal-out) is defined relative to SETTLE already, so nothing else needed to change -- same pattern the original v140 timing fix used.

changes: Deep tested on 2 real devices: intro plays, gold arc "YOUR CINEMA, EVERYWHERE" text appears correctly, but the letter-scramble/flicker effect before it never showed -- text just popped straight to final form. Root cause: some browser engines don't repaint a <tspan> textContent mutation inside an SVG <textPath> until something else forces text layout to recompute. changelog.title: Fix: Settings page could scroll horizontally on any phone -- flexbox min-width trap
changes: Found while building the First-Time Setup Help Guide GIF: measured document.documentElement.scrollWidth at 729px on a 414px mobile viewport -- the Settings page genuinely scrolled sideways. Root cause was the classic CSS flexbox trap: a flex item's default min-width is auto (its own max-content size), not 0 -- .settings-row-text (holding long unbroken strings like the real-debrid.com/apitoken links) refused to shrink below that width, so every one of the ~18 rows on the page pushed wider than the screen. Fixed with min-width:0 + overflow-wrap:anywhere on .settings-row-text and flex-shrink:0 on the row's button so it can't get squeezed either. Verified live: scrollWidth now matches the viewport, no horizontal scroll anywhere on the page.

changes: Reported by Deep: Cinema Finder not working. Root cause was systemic, not specific to Cinema Finder -- a plain Android WebView silently drops window.open() entirely unless setSupportMultipleWindows is on AND WebChromeClient.onCreateWindow is implemented. changelog.title: Real APK fix: nested-video fullscreen (South Park alt-source and any other embedded player)
changes: Reported by Deep via Telegram (photo: VK player's fullscreen/expand icon doing nothing). Root cause: MainActivity.kt used a bare WebChromeClient() which never implements onShowCustomView/onHideCustomView -- the standard Android WebView callback for native HTML5 video fullscreen. Any nested iframe's own fullscreen button (South Park's VK alt-source, or any other embedded player) silently did nothing, regardless of anything in the web app itself.

Fixed with a proper WebChromeClient override: mounts the fullscreen surface WebView hands us over the app's root view, hides the system status/nav bars for the duration (WindowInsetsControllerCompat), and restores everything cleanly on exit.

This is a genuine native Android source change -- unlike every other fix tonight (all web-content-only, picked up automatically via the service worker), this one needed a real new APK build. versionCode 23->24, versionName 0.1.25->0.1.26. Verified: gradle compile clean, release APK built and signed with the existing keystore (same cert, so this installs as an update over the current app, not a fresh install).

changelog.title: The actual root cause of the missing-posters saga -- a card frozen at 7.5% opacity
changes: Found via Deep's own DevTools inspection (real evidence, not another guess): a poster card was stuck at opacity: 0.0754 -- 25+ minutes after loading, confirmed not a network/loading issue. Cause: the intro's one-shot entrance animation (gsap.from on '.section.active .card', fading cards in from opacity 0) targets whatever cards exist the instant the intro finishes -- but card population is async, so a backgrounded tab (pausing GSAP's animation ticker mid-tween) or an overlapping re-render can freeze that fade-in permanently, with no way for it to ever recover on its own.

Added a deterministic safety net: 2 seconds after the intro completes, every card's GSAP-controlled opacity/transform is force-cleared back to its real CSS state, regardless of whether the entrance animation finished cleanly or got stuck. A stuck tween can now never leave a poster invisible again.

This was the actual bug behind everything reported in this thread tonight (posters missing on load, gaps while scrolling, one dimmed card that looked like slow loading) -- the earlier hydratePosters (v90) and skeleton-placeholder (v91) fixes were real improvements but neither was the root cause; this is.

changelog.title: Skeleton loading placeholders -- Home no longer shows blank space while content loads
changes: Real bug from Deep's screenshots: trendingGrid and continueWatchingGrid (and every genre-rail grid) are genuinely EMPTY -- zero children -- until their TMDB fetch resolves. No fallback content existed, so a slow network hop read as a broken blank void rather than "still loading". Added a shimmer skeleton placeholder shown immediately at page init, before any populate call fires; the real content overwrites it the moment it arrives, same as any other (re)render.

Not the same bug as the earlier hydratePosters fix (v90) -- that one was about individual posters missing inside cards that already existed. This one is about whole sections being missing entirely while their own network call is in flight.

changelog.title: 3 real fixes that shipped without a version bump -- this closes that gap
changes: hydratePosters() ran a full TMDB title-search per card SEQUENTIALLY (await inside a for-loop), with no skip for cards that already had a poster from the initial fetch -- a 20-30 card grid could take many seconds to finish, one card at a time. Now runs concurrently (Promise.all) and skips cards that already have a real poster.

The header widget row (VPN status, Proton launch, Profile switching, Watch Together, Sleep Timer) was unconditionally hidden below both 1300px and 900px viewport width -- meaning all 5 of those were completely unreachable on ANY phone-width screen, including this app. VPN status now stays visible and compact even at true phone width; the other 4 come back compact in the 900-1300px tablet range.

These three fixes were real and already deployed server-side, but never got a version bump when shipped -- meaning the app had no way to know they existed even after a manual reload. Same mistake as the WebView cache-bust fix earlier the same day, just for the web build number instead of the Android one. Bumping the version is now checked on every ship, not just native rebuilds.

changelog.title: WebView disk-cache fix -- app was serving stale content on cold launch
changes: Fixed a real bug found live: Deep's phone was showing stale app content after server updates, even though curl proved the server was serving the latest build correctly. Root cause was the Android WebView's own disk cache reusing an old lounge.html on cold launch. Added a cache-busting query param to the entry-point loadUrl() call.

This is the SECOND build of this fix -- the first (same day) shipped without a version bump, which meant old and new binaries were both indistinguishable as "0.1.24 build 22". Bumping the version is now part of the fix itself, not a formality, so this can't happen again.

Also ships (web-only, already live before this build): Simkl watch-history sync alongside Trakt, intro sting audio, Sky Sport EPG cloud fallback (fixes Now/Next strip going dark off-LAN), and a fix for posters missing on first paint above the fold.

changelog.title: Web-only: Trakt link fix + public-deploy PIN gate (no Android changes, still 0.1.24/22)
changes: Fixed the Trakt.tv Sync settings link -- it pointed at a dead legacy URL (app.trakt.tv/oauth/applications) that redirects to a blank apps list. Now points at app.trakt.tv/settings/apps/api/new, the current create-app form. Noted that an ad-blocker extension can leave that page blank (client-rendered SPA) -- try Incognito if so.

changelog.title: Trakt.tv sync, Skip Intro, multi-profile, offline download, watch-together
changes: Trakt.tv sync -- every movie/episode played pushes to your real Trakt watch history (device-code OAuth, no browser popup needed). Settings > Trakt.tv Sync. Requires your own free Trakt app (app.trakt.tv/oauth/applications).
Skip Intro -- mark where a show's intro ends once, every future episode of that show offers a Skip Intro button during the marked window. 'This device' player only.

Multi-profile ('Who's watching', header icon) -- watch history, favourite channels, intro marks and Continue Watching are now scoped per profile. Everything else (API keys, VPN/Trakt accounts, playback target) stays shared, on purpose. Existing data was migrated into a default 'Main' profile, nothing was lost.

Watch Together (header icon) -- share a 5-letter room code, someone else's Lounge mirrors your playback (position/pause state, polled every few seconds). 'This device' player only. Needs the cloud sync endpoint deployed -- ask Deep if this doesn't connect.
New LoungeNative.downloadMovie() bridge method backing offline download; WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permission added (API 28 and below only -- not needed or grantable on newer Android).

changelog.title: Proton VPN one-tap header button, sleep timer, HDR badge/filter
changes: Proton VPN launch moved out of a nested Settings popover into a one-tap button in the header, next to the VPN status chip -- same working launch call, just reachable in one tap instead of several plus a scroll.

New sleep timer (header clock icon) -- 15/30/45/60/90 min presets, stops the in-page player, mpv on the PC, or an active Cast session when it expires. Does not reach the native TV player (a separate Activity this page's JS can't see into while it's on top) -- stated in the timer's own popover, not silently unsupported.

Stream picker now detects and badges HDR releases (HDR/HDR10/HDR10+/Dolby Vision) separately from resolution -- a 2160p release can be SDR or HDR, they're independent attributes. New 'HDR only' filter chip alongside the existing (already-working) resolution tabs.
New LoungeNative.stopCast() bridge method, needed for the sleep timer to actually be able to stop a Cast session (castMedia() only ever loaded new media, there was no way to end one).

changelog.title: External Settings links + Restricted Area category links no longer dead taps in the app
changes: The Proton VPN button (Setup Guide + VPN popover) and 5 Settings links -- TMDB, Real-Debrid, Groq, OpenSubtitles, Plex -- all silently did nothing when tapped inside the packaged app. Root cause: MainActivity's shouldOverrideUrlLoading blocks any navigation off the configured Lounge host (correct, for JS-bridge security) but never launched an external Intent for what it blocks, so a plain link to an outside site just went nowhere -- it worked fine in a normal browser, which is why this wasn't caught earlier. Proton VPN now reuses the existing openVpnApp bridge; the other 5 route through a new general LoungeNative.openExternalBrowser(url), added specifically for this. Both fall back to a normal link tap outside the app, so nothing changes for browser/PWA use.

Restricted Area category tiles now open inside the app (embedded WebView with in-app Back navigation) instead of launching the system browser -- carried over from a completed but unshipped 2026-08-14 build.

changelog.title: Restricted Area really was broken this time -- crash on unlock, and the title mojibake was never actually fixed
changes: Entering the correct PIN in the Restricted Area crashed the screen outright. Cause: the category colours are written as 0xFF###### literals, which are bigger than Kotlin's Int range, so Kotlin silently treats them as Long -- and the code force-cast them to Int, which throws every single time. Android has no visible crash screen for this in a release build, so it just looked like the app bounced back to the intro. Fixed with an explicit Long-to-Int conversion, which is the correct way to read a 32-bit ARGB colour out of a literal like this.

The Restricted PIN dialog's title and PIN-box hint were still showing corrupted boxes -- the previous fix only touched the icons inside the screen itself, not this dialog, and the check used at the time could not have caught it (it scanned the wrong part of the build for this kind of text). Verified properly this time by reading the actual compiled screen inside the built file, not just the source.

changelog.title: Restricted Area was unreachable, intro spacing opened up
changes: The Restricted Area (RestrictedSectionActivity, PIN 69) was fully built but had no way to open it -- no menu item and no bridge call ever launched it, since whenever it was first added. Found live when Deep looked for it in a fresh install. Added a menu item under Tools (Android app only -- it has no web equivalent) and the missing native bridge call.
The intro's tagline arc sat almost flush against the couch mark, and the couch mark sat close above the 'Press Any Key to Take a Seat' button -- both opened up.

Looked into the 'Press Any Key' prompt not responding to a keypress on some device: the native/JS bridge that lets D-pad and keyboard events through during the intro is wired correctly on inspection. Not reproduced from source -- if this was tested on the phone build, there is no physical key to press and the click is the intentional fallback for that case, not a bug. Flagging rather than guessing at a fix for a mechanism that already looks correct.

changelog.title: Restricted section icons fixed, Proton VPN shortcut, stream source in the stats overlay
changes: The Restricted section's icons were rendering as replacement-character garbage on every tile, and the PIN dialog's title and input hint with them. Cause was an encoding fault in two source files, not the fonts: each icon had a duplicate emoji whose leading byte had been lost, leaving three orphan bytes the renderer drew as boxes. Both files re-saved as clean UTF-8 without a BOM so it does not come back.

Settings' VPN panel can now open Proton VPN in one tap, or its Play Store listing if it is not installed yet. To be exact about what this is: it is a shortcut, not an embedded VPN. Proton has no SDK anyone can build against (business partner programme, direct contact only), and Android would not allow it either -- a VPN tunnel only runs inside the process of the app that declares it, so no app can host another app's VPN. This removes the settings hunt and nothing more. It only appears in the Android app; a web page cannot see or launch an installed app.

The playback stats overlay (press I during playback) now names the source that resolved the stream you are watching -- Real-Debrid, a direct channel URL, or the cloud relay. Previously a stalled Real-Debrid link and a dead channel URL looked identical on screen.

A device two or more builds behind now gets one dismissible reminder on open instead of only the small badge, which was easy to never notice. It does not block anything, and it does not come back for a version gap you have already dismissed.

Picture-in-picture was checked on both players (the built-in one and the native VLC one) after the recent PC-independence rewrite. Both paths are still wired -- no changes were needed, and none were made.

changelog.title: VPN status chip in the nav bar
changes: A VPN status chip now sits in the top nav next to the weather/clock -- grey until you first check it (nothing runs silently, same privacy rule Settings' VPN panel already followed), then green/red based on whether your traffic looks different from a saved "normal connection" baseline. Click it for country, network operator, and a real measured latency (not a fake number).

Honest limit, stated in the panel itself: a web page cannot see or control a system VPN, on any platform. This reports the one thing that IS observable -- your public IP's country and operator -- compared against what you saved as normal. It is a comparison, not a true on/off VPN detector.

First click on the chip offers to keep it live (checks every 5 minutes while the tab is open) -- opt-in, not a silent default, for the same reason the original Settings panel never auto-checked on page load.

changelog.title: Cloud EPG + watch-history, Proton VPN swap, PC-independence complete
changes: Program guide (EPG) and Continue Watching/resume now work with your PC fully off, the same way Real-Debrid/Sky Sport/subtitles already did -- completing the migration started 2026-08-10. Both still prefer your PC's relay first when it's reachable (lower latency), falling back to the cloud automatically.

One-time setup needed on the Vercel side before the cloud paths activate -- see CLOUD_STORAGE_SETUP.md. Nothing changes for you until that's done; everything keeps working through your PC exactly as it does today in the meantime.

VPN recommendation for Android switched from Windscribe (10GB/month cap) to Proton VPN (no cap) -- same per-app routing mechanism, just a different app, after checking that Proton's free-tier "streaming block" reputation is specifically about Netflix-style IP-blocklisting and doesn't apply to Real-Debrid/DaddyLive traffic.
Fixed a stale claim in the VPN guide's Android TV panel that said no Lounge TV app existed yet -- it's existed since the versionCode 10 rename, this just hadn't been updated to say so.

changelog.title: Surprise Me, idle screensaver, shortcuts, playback stats, watchlist backup
changes: New "Surprise Me" shuffle -- a dice button (or the S key) picks a random title from whatever's already loaded on screen and opens it straight away, for when you don't know what to watch.
Idle ambient mode: leave Lounge open and untouched for 5 minutes and it fades into a slow crossfade of posters instead of sitting on a static screen. Any key, click, or touch brings it straight back.
Keyboard shortcuts cheatsheet -- press ? (or tap the new keyboard icon) to see every shortcut in one place instead of having to remember them.
Playback stats overlay (I key) for anyone who wants to see what's actually happening under the hood -- resolution, buffer health, playback state -- while something is playing.
My List can now be exported to a JSON file and re-imported -- a real backup before a device wipe or reinstall, since watchlist data lives only in this browser's storage.

changelog.title: PC-independent playback, and touch controls for the native player
changes: Real-Debrid, Sky Sport live TV, and subtitle fetching no longer need your PC on. Those calls used to go through nexus_control_relay.py running at home; they now go through a cloud relay, so watching works from anywhere, PC on or off.

The app itself (lounge.html) can now be loaded straight from the internet too, not just from your PC's local server -- so opening Lounge away from home no longer needs the PC reachable at all, for either the page or playback.

Fixed a routing bug found while testing the above: the cloud Real-Debrid proxy 404'd on any call with more than one path segment (adding a magnet, checking status, unrestricting a link) -- so live TV worked but movies silently failed with "Something went wrong resolving this stream" every time. Real-Debrid playback is now confirmed working end-to-end with the PC off.

The format-not-supported fallback (shown when a file's codec can't play in-browser) now offers "Play on this device (VLC)" ahead of "Play on Laptop (mpv)" when the native player is available -- previously it only ever suggested the PC, even on a device that could already play the file itself.

The native VLC player (used for MKV/AC3/HEVC files the browser can't decode) had no on-screen controls at all -- every control only worked via a TV remote's D-pad, so on a phone there was nothing to tap and the only way out was the Android BACK key. It now has a tap-to-show transport overlay: play/pause, +-10s skip, a seek bar with a time readout, and a close button. The TV remote's D-pad controls are unchanged.

changelog.title: Real fix for movies not playing
changes: Traced the "Something went wrong resolving this stream" error reported live today. Real-Debrid now rejects a magnet link that has no filename attached to it as a copyright violation - regardless of what the content actually is. This app always built magnets without a filename, so this had likely been silently breaking some fraction of plays for a while, not just tonight and not just Bollywood titles - proven by testing the exact same torrent hash both ways: bare hash was blocked even for a decades-old, completely uncontroversial film; the identical hash with a filename attached went through immediately.
Magnets built by this app now carry a filename and a small set of trackers, the same way a normal torrent file would.

Honest limit: this does not make every title playable. A handful of very new, high-profile releases are genuinely blocked by Real-Debrid on purpose, filename or not - that's Real-Debrid's own policy, not something this app can route around. If one source on a title fails, try another - they're graded independently.

changelog.title: A way back when the page crashes, not just when it fails to load
changes: The black screen with just a small Android icon in the corner, reported live today, was not the app failing to reach the server - it's what the system shows when the page's own renderer process dies. None of the app's previous recovery screens could appear for this, because they all needed the page to still be alive to trigger them.

The app now catches that specific crash, rebuilds the page fresh, and shows a real message with the same tap-to-open-Settings option as a normal connection failure - instead of a silent black screen with nothing to press.

Honest limit: this does not explain why the renderer crashed in the first place. That needs a device log this app can't collect on its own. It guarantees there's always a way back to Settings when it happens, not that it won't happen again.

changelog.title: Fresh installs now just work, home or away
changes: 0.1.13's fix (tap the error message to reach Settings) still needed the page to fail first and needed that tap to actually be found and to work - and a real test away from home still did not open. Rather than add a third recovery path, the app no longer needs one: a brand new install now points at the internet address (the same Cloudflare Tunnel used for the APK downloads) instead of the PC's local network address by default.

This means installing the app away from home now works immediately, with no Settings step. At home, it's one extra hop out to the internet and back instead of talking to the PC directly on the LAN - a small tradeoff for an install that just opens.
The old local-network address is still available - open Settings and enter it there for anyone who wants the more direct path while on the home WiFi.

changelog.title: Real-Debrid is now optional, and Plex can be signed in
changes: Real-Debrid is no longer treated as a requirement. Opening any film or episode used to check for a Real-Debrid key first and stop dead with "Add your Real-Debrid API key in Settings first" if it was missing, so letting the subscription lapse would have taken the whole app down with it. Playback sources are now a list: if one is missing, the rest still get used.
Clearing the Real-Debrid box in Settings and pressing Save now actually removes the key. It previously ignored an empty box, so there was no way to switch Real-Debrid off from the screen.

Without a debrid service, the torrent scrapers are skipped instead of searched. They only ever return magnet links, which need a debrid to become something a player can open, so listing them would have filled the screen with results that cannot play.
New "Playback Sources" panel in Settings shows, with a dot per source, which ones are set up and what each one can resolve. Live TV and Live Sports need none of them and are noted as such.

You can sign in to Plex from Settings. It shows a 4-character code to enter at plex.tv/link and picks up the sign-in on its own once you do. Plex's free Movies & Shows catalogue does not need Plex Pass, but it does need a free Plex account - there is no anonymous access.
Not done yet: signing in stores the token, but Lounge does not search or play Plex titles yet. That part is unbuilt and untested.

Checked and rejected: ThreeNow cannot be added. Every stream it serves is DRM-locked (FairPlay, Widevine and PlayReady on all 8 variants of the episode tested), so this app's player physically cannot open one. TVNZ+ has no reachable public API - every address tried was refused by their gateway.

changelog.title: Fixed: a fresh install away from home had no way in
changes: A phone installing this app for the first time away from home WiFi loaded the PC's local address by default, couldn't reach it, and the error screen's only advice was "Press MENU on the remote" - which doesn't exist on a phone. There was no way to reach Settings at all in that state.
That error message is now tappable and opens Settings directly.
Settings has a new "Use Lounge Cloud" button that fills in the internet address for both the app and the control relay in one tap, instead of typing two long addresses on a phone keyboard.

changelog.title: Six country tabs, and a PIN-locked section
changes: Live TV now loads five countries instead of two. New Zealand and Australia were already there; India, the USA and the UK have been added, which takes the channel list from 92 to roughly 2,500.
One-tap country buttons sit above the grid: NZ, AUS, INDIA, USA and UK. Tap one to see only that country, tap it again to go back to everything.
Programme guide data now loads for India, the USA and the UK as well, so the genre filters and the Now/Next strip work on those channels the same way they already did for NZ and Australia.

Fiji was asked for and is wired up, but no Fiji button appears yet. The free channel source lists nine Fiji channels and publishes no working stream for any of them, so there is nothing that would actually play. The app checks for them every few hours and the button will appear on its own if that ever changes.

New Restricted section. Each channel card has a padlock in its top corner; press it to move that channel out of the normal grid. Restricted channels are hidden from both Live TV and Live Sports until you tap the Restricted button and enter the PIN. It starts empty — you choose what goes in it.
The Restricted PIN keeps people from stumbling into those channels on a shared TV. It is not real security: anyone who knows their way around a browser can get past it.

changelog.title: It tells you when there's an update
changes: Every device now checks for updates on its own: phone, PC, Google TV, Android TV and Fire Stick all read the same version file, so none of them can quietly sit on an old build again.
When something newer exists you get an Update badge on Settings, and this panel opens with the actual list of what changed and a button that fetches it.
Settings now shows exactly which build you are running — app version and version code on Android, web build number in a browser.
New "What's New" section in Settings so you can re-read any release, not just the newest one.

New "Where your traffic leaves from" panel in Settings: it reads the public address the internet actually sees you from and names the network operator behind it. Save your normal connection once and it will tell you when the current one looks different — which is the honest limit of what a web page can know about a VPN.

changelog.title: Picture-in-picture, a real player bar, and Australian channels
changes: Picture-in-picture: press HOME while something is playing and it shrinks to a floating window that keeps playing while you use other apps. Works for both the built-in player and the native one, and the little window has its own play/pause button.

The "This device" player got its own transport bar. The browser's stock white play button and its complete absence of a subtitle control are gone — seek, play/pause and subtitles are the app's own now.

Australian Live TV channels. Lounge only ever loaded New Zealand's channel list, so there was no filter that could have found an Australian channel — they were never fetched. Both lists now load (31 NZ + 79 AU entries, merged by stream address into 92 unique channels because 18 were the same feed listed twice).
NZ and AUS quick-filter buttons on Live TV and Live Sports.
Coming Soon stopped after the first page of results and said it could not load more, while the source still had 167 more pages for the same search. Fixed.
The highlight capsule under the Live TV filter buttons was invisible until you tapped one. It is now in the right place the moment the page opens.

changelog.title: The round from your phone screenshots
changes: The top bar no longer hides under your phone's status bar. The hamburger menu button was being rendered underneath the system clock, which is why it looked missing — it was there, just untappable.

BACK works properly. It used to close the whole app from anywhere, including mid-film. It now closes whatever is actually on top: the format warning, the player, live TV, the source picker, the menu drawer, then the detail page.
BACK twice to leave. One press warns, a second within two seconds exits, so you cannot lose your place by accident.
New app icon. The launcher was still showing the old Nexus "N"; it is now the couch-and-popcorn mark, drawn at every screen density.
"Watch Now" and "Resume" now use the popcorn play button like the rest of the app instead of a plain triangle.

changelog.title: One app for phone, Google TV and Fire Stick
changes: The app would not install on a phone at all. It declared itself TV-only, which made the Play services filter it off phone hardware entirely. One build now covers phone, Google TV, Android TV and Fire Stick.
Added a normal app-drawer icon. The TV-launcher entry alone gave no icon on a phone.
The screen stays in portrait while you browse, and flips to landscape only for video.

The remote works. Every tile and menu item in this app is a plain div, which a TV remote physically cannot move focus between — arrow keys used to reach nothing. Lounge now works out which tile is nearest in the direction you pressed and highlights it.
The app is signed with a permanent key, so future updates install over the top instead of asking you to uninstall first.
